newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end higher on ending stocks estimate.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end higher on ending stocks estimate.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended higher on short covering triggered by news some analysts had cut ending stocks projections, traders said.
"The Dean Witter analyst put out a 125 million bean carryout and that got in the market," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Dean Witter analyst Jerry Gidel told Reuters he projected ending stocks at 125 million bushels although he added that USDA would probably put the number closer to 140 million. Gidel's estimate included crush usage 20 million bushels above USDA's current figure and exports 10 million bushels higher.
USDA on Wednesday will release its supply/demand report. Last month USDA cut its soybean ending stocks estimate to 155 million bushels from 180 million a month earlier.
Fund buying late in the session lent support. Rosenthal Collins bought at least five million bushels March on the day, traders said.
Good growing conditions in South America capped gains. Conditions were stable in Brazil's key soybean growing region with growers expecting some rain over the weekend.
Soybeans ended eight cents per bushel higher to one cent lower with March up eight at $7.38.
Technically, the market found support below $7.30 per bushel in the March and closed above the four-day moving average of $7.36. Resistance was pegged at $7.41-1/2.
In options trade, Cargill Investor Services reportedly bought 300 May $7.50 calls at 12 cents and sold 300 March $7.25 calls at 10-1/2 cents, traders said.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 47,000 contracts, against Thursday's actual volume of 56,182 contracts.
